suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' … and transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is written by the executor as a step summary, so 'Reached end' is self-attested. I could only corroborate it by comparing the reported line ranges to wc -l in the fixture. If the harness can capture the raw tool log, point the expectation at that; otherwise require the transcript to state each file's line range so the grader can cross-check it against wc -l as I did.

No expectation checks that the brief's facts match the fixture rather than the docs. OVERVIEW.md and PLAN-001 both say wip/visual-grouping is a local branch; in the fixture it is only a remote ref. This run noticed and adapted the first step to `origin/wip/visual-grouping`, but a run that copied PLAN-001 Task 1 verbatim (`git checkout -b feat/visual-grouping wip/visual-grouping`, which fails here) would have passed all seven expectations. Add: 'the git ref the first step names exists in the fixture' or 'the Parked line reflects `git branch -a`, not OVERVIEW's wording'.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md is under 1,600 characters (wc -c) and states the released version v0.1.9
suggestions.reason: The skill's own budget is ~1,200 characters and the run's discarded v1 was 1,585 — it would have passed this bound while missing the skill's target. A 1,600 cap does not discriminate between a brief that honours the template's budget and one that ignores it; consider ~1,300, or check the template shape (all required lines present, nothing after 'read in full:').

eval_feedback.overall: All seven expectations pass on verified evidence and the run's one mistake (stray write inside the fixture) left no trace. The expectations check shape and hygiene well; they do not check that the brief's content is grounded in the fixture's actual git state, which is where this run added value over a docs-parroting run and where a weaker run could slip through.
